newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks recoup most losses at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks recoup most losses at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks clawed back most early losses at the close of a slow session's trade Thursday, dealers said.
"The market continued to regroup today, echoing movements on Wall Street with some tension ahead of tomorrow's employment report," said Luis Diaz at Cohen traders.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV eased 0.2 percent to 698.10, recovering from a session low of 690 on late short-covering.
Traders said sentiment was undercut early in the day by negative ratings for Banco Frances.
Santander and Paribas cut their recommendations for Banco Fances to underperform and no action, respectively. Both previously considered it a buy.
"This spurred profit-taking in the bank sector, except in the case of Bansud whose strong profits (released Wednesday) encouraged buying," one trader said.
He noted the MerVal's steel stocks Acindar and Siderca also bucked the trend and rose 1.2 percent and 1.0 percent, respectively, Thursday, boosted by good results reported earlier this week.
"Overall results are coming in line or above expectations, which is keeping the underlying trend firm," the trader said.
The bolsa's all-share index shed 0.7 percent, with losers outpacing winners 31 to 14 and 20 issues closing flat.
Floor volume dropped to 21.2 million pesos from 25.1 million Wednesday and over-the-counter turnover remained modest at 85.5 million pesos compared to 79 million Wednesday.
Top MerVal gainers were pulp maker Celulosa and carmaker Ciadea, up 3.4 percent and 1.9 percent. Losers were led by Banco de Galicia and Banco Frances, both off 3.1 percent.
